newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's ISS says no dividend for 96.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's ISS says no dividend for 96.

text.p: Danish cleaning group International Service System (ISS) said on Friday that it would recommend to shareholders that no dividend be paid for 1996 because of a two billion crown loss incurred by irregularities in its U.S. subsidiary.

"The group's financial situation, which has been affected by the heavy loss in ISS Inc in 1996 means that the group's board will recommend to shareholders at the annual general meeting in April that no dividend be paid for 1996," a statement said.

It added that the sale of ISS Inc to Canada's Aaxis Ltd, announced last December, had since been finalised at a price of one U.S. dollar and 313,598 Aaxis shares -- a 19.5 percent shareholding worth about 2.9 million Canadian dollars.
The deal includes a five-year agreement under which ISS Inc will continue to operate under the ISS name and logo in North and South America.
The statement said that ISS group contingent liabilities would be reduced by 160 million U.S dollars as a result of the sale.

The two sides also signed an option agreement for the purchase of the ISS group's Brazilian subsidiary, at a price to be fixed at the time the option is exercised, which can be up to one year after the completion of the unit's 1996 accounts.
ISS shares were virtually unmoved by the announcements, slipping one crown to 146 crowns by 1020 GMT. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
